issues.title: cli/plan.go:429 still emits an em-dash in a new user-facing stderr line (planGo's unresolved-target message)
issues.description: The plan's cross-cutting invariants say 'no em-dash' and REV-003 (review round 1) fixed three user-facing status strings for exactly this. One new user-facing string was missed: cli/plan.go:429, inside the new `planGo` (FR3 re-sequence) - `fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "gogo plan go: target %q is not a source of %q — skipping\n", target, project)` uses U+2014. Confirmed live via the real binary: `gogo plan go <id>` on a plan with an unresolved target (a `targets:` entry that is not a project source) prints this line verbatim to stderr, em-dash and all. Cosmetic only - the command still exits non-zero and names the target correctly (TestCmdPlanGoInvalidTargetsReported passes because it only asserts substrings 'ghost' and 'unresolved', not the exact separator character).
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE: replace the em-dash with ' - ' at cli/plan.go:429, matching the three strings REV-003 already fixed (planMarkReady, planGo's no-targets message, viewPlanDetail's awaiting-uat cue). One-line change; no test currently pins the character so none needs updating, though a follow-up could assert `!strings.ContainsRune(out, '\u2014')` on this stderr line to prevent recurrence.
issues.fix_summary: Swapped the em-dash for ' - ' in planGo's unresolved-target stderr line (plan.go). gofmt/vet/-race green.
